subject: Dedicated GPU pool pricing + load-test results to size commit
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex@nimbus.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated pool inquiry + load test request

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. We're evaluating a Dedicated GPU pool to serve our customer-facing LLM feature (multi-turn chat + tool calls). Target traffic: ~200–300 TPS peak for inference requests during MLP rollouts and sustained ~80–120 TPS off-peak. P95 latency target is <=400ms for single-stream responses.

Before we talk contract terms we want a load test and a sizing recommendation from Redwood so we can justify a reserved commit to finance. Can your team run a 48-hour sustained test (realistic prompt distribution attached) and share TPS traces, p95/p99 latency, and KV-cache hit assumptions?

I've attached our load profile CSV (nimbus-load-profile.csv). Procurement will also want a basic pricing estimate and any volume discount thresholds.

Alex
Alex Moreno
Head of Platform
NimbusAI

Attachments: nimbus-load-profile.csv (CSV)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool inquiry + load test request

Alex — thanks for the profile and the clarity on TPS/latency targets. We can run the 48-hour run and provide a recommended commit size plus a pricing tier that maps to throughput SLOs.

Plan:
- Connor will own the load-test harness and provide the raw traces + a condensed CSV (tps + latency percentiles).
- We'll produce two sizing options: (A) cost-optimized commit that meets 95% of your peak windows, (B) SLO-backed commit sized for 99% of peak.
- We'll include discount levels tied to 12/24-month reserved commits and a short mutual action plan for procurement.

Next step: Connor, can you spin up a mirror test this week using their profile? Marissa — I'll loop you in for pricing/discounts.

Best,
Vanessa
Senior Sales Director, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Moreno <alex@nimbus.ai>
Date: 2026-10-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool inquiry + load test request

Vanessa / Marissa / Alex —

We've started an initial 24-hour run on a staging Dedicated pool that mirrors the 0.75x–1.0x request distribution you sent. Quick observations from the first 6 hours:
- Sustained throughput: ~260 TPS during simulated peak bursts (10-min windows).
- P95 latency: 310–380ms depending on sequence length; P99 spikes to ~620ms during cold KV-cache windows.
- KV cache hit rate in this harness averaged 68% after warm-up; with a priming run it's >80% which materially reduces p99.

Sizing recommendation (preliminary):
- Cost-opt (Option A): 4 x H100-equivalent slots (reserved) -> expected sustained 220–260 TPS with p95 < 400ms and 24/7 coverage.
- SLO-backed (Option B): 6 x H100-equivalent slots -> headroom for 300+ TPS peaks and p99 < 500ms with KV priming and automated burst capacity.

Notes: these numbers assume continuous batching with a per-request average of ~420 tokens and use our quantization profile. If Nimbus expects longer sequences or heavier tool-call throughput, step up one slot.

I've uploaded raw traces + a condensed CSV: nimbus-loadtest-2026-10-28.csv and tps-trace-plot.png. Also attaching a draft pool-sizing workbook.

Connor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: nimbus-loadtest-2026-10-28.csv (CSV), tps-trace-plot.png (PNG), pool-sizing-v1.xlsx (XLSX)
From: Alex Moreno <alex@nimbus.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@nimbus.ai>
Date: 2026-10-30T08:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool inquiry + load test request

Connor — thanks for the fast turnaround and the artifacts. The numbers look reasonable. A few follow-ups from my side and procurement:

1) Can Redwood commit to a throughput SLO (e.g., 99% of requests served under 500ms) for Option B if we take a 12-month reserved commit? We'd like an SLA we can pass to customers.
2) We are targeting a 12-month reserved commit but we'll need a 20% discount relative to list Dedicated pricing to meet our internal ROI thresholds. Is that possible at the proposed commit size?
3) Procurement asked about burst capacity: if we hit >350 TPS sustained for 30+ minutes, what's the automatic fallback or burst policy (and cost)?

If those three items are workable we'll prepare an internal sign-off and loop legal.

Alex

Attachments: none
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@nimbus.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool inquiry + load test request

Alex / team —

Thanks for the close read. Quick responses to the three asks:

1) Throughput SLOs: For Option B (6-slot pool) we can commit to a latency SLO of 99% under 500ms for inference-only traffic with standard KV priming and recommended batching. This SLO will be contingent on an agreed token-distribution and request-size profile (your attached profile) and a 12-month reserved commit. We'll tie regression monitoring and a monthly report to the SLO.

2) Pricing/discounts: We can do a 20% effective discount if Nimbus signs a 12-month reserved commit at the Option B level and agrees to a quarterly usage review. Alternate: 12% discount for Option A (4-slot) 12-month commit. We'll provide a formal pricing schedule; see attached commit-pricing-tier.pdf for the draft bands and included burst credits.

3) Burst policy: automatic burst capacity is available up to +50% sustained for 30 minutes (subject to available capacity); bursts beyond that will throttle to the committed pool and optionally invoke pay-as-you-go overflow. We'll include explicit burst credits in the 12-month Option B offer to cover expected spike windows.

Caveats: For tool-heavy flows with external API waits, the effective concurrency differs; we'll add a short annex to the SLA describing those cases. Also the p99 during cold cache will remain higher; our recommended onboarding includes a priming run prior to major launches.

I'll have Legal/Commercial convert these bullets into contract language; Vanessa / Marissa, please prepare the formal quote and MOP.

-Karthik
VP Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: commit-pricing-tier.pdf (PDF)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@nimbus.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool inquiry + load test request

Alex / Procurement —

Great — sounds like we're aligned. Summary / mutual action plan:
- Option selected: Option B (6-slot H100-equivalent pool) with 12-month reserved commit.
- Commercials: 20% discount on list Dedicated pricing (see attached draft) in exchange for 12-month commit and quarterly usage reviews.
- SLO: 99% < 500ms (inference-only) tied to agreed profile and priming. Monthly SLO reports and a one-time onboarding priming run before go-live.
- Burst: up to +50% for 30 minutes automatic; additional overflow at PAYG with burst credits included in first quarter.
- Next steps: Procurement to confirm PO template and legal to accept SLA annex. We will deliver final quote + redlined MSA within 48 hours.

Can Procurement confirm target PO date and any billing/legal constraints? If we get a PO by 2026-11-10 we can schedule onboarding the week of 2026-11-17.

Thanks — Vanessa

Attachments: final-quote-draft.pdf (to follow)
